Growth & demand: According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) World Economic Outlook Update (July 2026), global economic growth is projected at 3.0% in 2026, before improving modestly to 3.4% in 2027 , compared with an average growth rate of 3.5% during 2024-25.

Margins & costs: We reported Revenue from Operations of ₹53.23 crore, EBITDA of ₹10.31 crore and Profit After Tax of ₹6.48 crore, while continuing to maintain healthy operating margins.

Although revenue declined during the period, PAT margin improved from 11.1% to 12.6%, demonstrating that management maintained pricing discipline and profitability despite a more challenging operating environment.
The facility operated at approximately 85% capacity utilisation during FY2026, reflecting healthy utilisation levels while retaining capacity to support future demand growth.
Capex & expansion: With an installed manufacturing capacity of 33,500 industrial and marine valves and 85% capacity utilisation, the facility supports both current production requirements and future growth.
Employee benefit expenses increased as a percentage of revenue from 3.9% to 5.3%, reflecting continued investment in manufacturing capabilities and organisational capacity.

Out of the IPO proceeds, ₹764.51 Lakhs remained unutilised, comprising ₹364.51 Lakhs originally earmarked towards capital expenditure for purchase of new plant and machin- ery and software and ₹400.00 Lakhs towards pursu- ing inorganic growth initiatives through acquisitions.
Balance sheet & cash: Inventories increased to ₹2,667.5 Lakhs, while trade receivables rose to ₹2,483.2 Lakhs, reflecting inventory build-up and project execution requirements during the year.
Debt Equity Ratio 0.35x 0.19x 84.2% The increase primarily reflects higher short-term borrowings undertaken to support working capital requirements during the year.

DIVIDEND & RESERVES Declaration and payment of Dividend In order to conserve financial resources for meeting the Company's long-term working capital require- ments and supporting its future growth and expan- sion plans, the Board of Directors has decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.
Risks & challenges: Volatility in copper and other non-ferrous metal prices, together with temporary supply chain disruptions arising from geopolitical developments, created uncertainty across procurement and project execution.

The first half of the year benefited from favourable operating conditions and healthy project execution, whereas the second half was characterised by heightened raw material volatility, supply chain disruptions and geopolitical uncertainty.
